Our findings suggest that targeted HIV testing interventions are necessary to reduce disparities in HIV testing among Black and Hispanic populations.

medical image analysis is heavily reliant on the quality of training data. However, the high cost of manual annotation by medical professionals poses a significant challenge. To address this issue, we propose a semi-supervised learning approach that utilizes weakly annotated images to train a semantic segmentation model. Our method involves a novel attention-based module that identifies and highlights areas of interest within images, thereby facilitating the creation of precise masks from weakly annotated images. By combining these masks with strongly labeled data, we develop a robust training dataset for semantic segmentation. Our approach was successfully tested on the segmentation of brain tumors in MRI images, demonstrating its potential to enhance the performance of deep learning models using weakly annotated images.
